findings.title: Third-party GitHub Actions pinned by tag, not SHA; no explicit permissions block
findings.description: pnpm/action-setup@v4 (line 28, also 76) and supabase/setup-cli@v1 (line 36) are third-party actions pinned by mutable tag. actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, actions/setup-python@v5, actions/upload-artifact@v4 are first-party (MEDIUM by FP rule). The workflow has no top-level permissions: block, so the default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions apply on push builds.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Attacker compromises the pnpm/action-setup or supabase/setup-cli repo or its tag. 2) Re-points the v4/v1 tag at a malicious commit. 3) Next CI run on this repo executes attacker code on the runner with the default GITHUB_TOKEN, which without a permissions: block can have contents write on push builds - enough to push commits or tamper with artifacts.
findings.impact: Supply-chain code execution in CI; possible repo write via default GITHUB_TOKEN. No repository secrets are exposed in this workflow (only local dev values), which limits blast radius.
findings.recommendation: Pin third-party actions to full commit SHAs (uses: pnpm/action-setup@<sha> # v4). Add a top-level 'permissions: contents: read' block to ci.yml. Optionally add CODEOWNERS on .github/workflows/.
findings.verification: self-verified - lines read directly; no repo secrets referenced anywhere in the workflow

findings.title: Committed dev password 'app_pw' + [db.seed] enabled = true leaves a live path to reseeding an internet-reachable preview DB with a known password
findings.description: supabase/seed.sql ends with: alter role aktflow_app_login password 'app_pw'; and supabase/config.toml:62 has [db.seed] enabled = true. The repo's own comments (seed.sql, 0003_roles_and_grants.sql, ci.yml, .env.example) document that supabase db push --include-seed, supabase db reset --linked --include-seed, and Supabase Branching preview branches (automatically, no flag) all apply seed.sql. aktflow_app membership is full tenant-table read/write. The documented mitigation ('set [db.seed] enabled = false before enabling Branching') is procedural only; the safe default is not applied and nothing enforces it.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Team later enables Supabase Branching (or an operator runs a documented-forbidden --include-seed command against a hosted project). 2) The preview/hosted DB is reseeded, setting aktflow_app_login's password to the public value 'app_pw' on an internet-reachable pooler endpoint. 3) Anyone who read this public-repo-style file connects as aktflow_app_login, does set role aktflow_app, sets app.actor_user_id to any value, and reads/writes every tenant table (RLS policies key off a self-declared GUC for this trusted role).
findings.impact: Full cross-tenant read/write on any database where seed.sql is ever applied while reachable. Currently conditional: the default staging/prod path (plain supabase db push) does not apply seed.sql.
findings.recommendation: Remove the password statement from seed.sql entirely. Set the dev/CI password out-of-band instead: a make target or a psql step in ci.yml and local setup (psql "$SUPABASE_DB_URL" -c "alter role aktflow_app_login password 'app_pw'") that Supabase tooling can never auto-apply. Alternatively at minimum flip [db.seed] enabled = false and pass seed explicitly where needed. This converts a documented do-not-run rule into a structural impossibility.
findings.playbook: If seed.sql is ever applied to a hosted project: 1) alter role aktflow_app_login password to a fresh secret immediately; 2) audit pg_stat_activity / connection logs for aktflow_app_login logins during the exposure window; 3) review audit_events for unexpected writes.
findings.verification: self-verified - both motivating lines quoted; application paths confirmed from Supabase CLI behavior documented consistently across four files in the repo

notes.scope_reality: External-link protocol and object storage have NO runtime implementation at HEAD abdad52 - they exist only as target design in docs/architecture/. This audit covers the actual runtime slice: supabase/migrations 0001-0005, seed.sql, config.toml, apps/app auth + 2 API routes, packages/database, packages/testing RLS suite, .github/workflows/ci.yml. Target-doc claims were NOT audited as if implemented.
positive_observations: RLS policies deny-by-default: UPDATE/DELETE have no policies on tenant tables, so they are blocked despite table grants
withTenantTx sets GUCs via parameterized set_config and set local role inside a transaction; nothing leaks to the pooled connection
requireUser validates tokens server-side via auth.getUser() on both bearer and cookie paths; never trusts client-supplied user ids
le_insert policy closes cross-tenant legal-entity injection; m_insert bootstrap is race-safe because org+membership commit atomically and the org UUID is unguessable pre-commit
withIdempotency uses pg_advisory_xact_lock + request-hash conflict detection; replay window surfaced via header
0003/0005 explicitly strip Supabase default-privilege grants from anon/authenticated and revoke EXECUTE on drain_outbox from browser roles
Negative RLS tests exist (packages/testing/src/rls.test.ts): cross-tenant select, membership self-insert, legal-entity injection
No secrets in git history; no tracked .env files; CI uses only local dev values
below_gate_observations: config.toml minimum_password_length=6, password_requirements empty - local dev config; hosted project auth settings are managed separately; tighten before real users
audit_events/transaction_outbox/idempotency_records have no RLS (grants-only protection for trusted BFF role) - acknowledged in-slice by design comments; carry to target v0.1 catalogs
